name: 01-open-surfmeter
title: Find your way around SurfMeter
kind: Native SwiftUI render · sample activity · controls shown for reference

notes.title: Open Browser setup
notes.text: Click the globe in the footer. This is where you connect Chrome and enable recording.

notes.title: Open Preferences
notes.text: Use the gear for login items, appearance, retention, exclusions, and activity deletion.

notes.title: Pause or resume
notes.text: This stops or resumes recording without deleting previously recorded activity.

notes.title: Choose your period
notes.text: Daily includes a Yesterday shortcut. Weekly shows the last seven calendar days.

name: 02-load-chrome
title: Load the Chrome extension
kind: Google Chrome documentation screenshot · Hello Extensions example, not SurfMeter

notes.title: Turn on Developer mode
notes.text: Open chrome://extensions and enable this switch to reveal the local extension controls.

notes.title: Choose Load unpacked
notes.text: Select SurfMeter's ChromeExtension folder, or extensions/chrome/dist in the checkout. Select the folder containing manifest.json.

notes.title: Copy YOUR extension ID
notes.text: Copy the ID from the SurfMeter — Browser Bridge card. The Hello Extensions ID in this example must not be reused.

notes.title: Leave the extension enabled
notes.text: Keep SurfMeter's switch on. If the card is missing, check the folder you loaded and any manifest errors.

name: 03-register-chrome
title: Register the local Chrome connection
kind: Native setup content render · before connection · preview buttons are disabled

notes.title: Reveal the bundled folder
notes.text: In the real app this opens Finder at ChromeExtension. Use this folder with Chrome's Load unpacked command.

notes.title: Paste the actual Chrome ID
notes.text: Use the 32-letter ID from your SurfMeter extension card, not a sample ID or the whole chrome-extension URL.

notes.title: Choose Connect Chrome
notes.text: This registers the per-user native helper for that exact extension ID. Recording remains off until you enable it.

name: 04-pin-chrome
title: Pin and reconnect the extension
kind: Google Chrome documentation screenshot · choose SurfMeter instead of Hello Extensions

notes.title: Open the Extensions menu
notes.text: Click Chrome's puzzle icon. Find SurfMeter — Browser Bridge in the extension list.

notes.title: Pin SurfMeter, then click it
notes.text: Pin the SurfMeter row for easy access. Open a normal web page, then click SurfMeter's toolbar icon to reconnect.

name: 05-enable-recording
title: Enable recording after Chrome connects
kind: Native setup content render · scroll down in the actual popover to reach these controls

notes.title: Enable eligible Chrome recording
notes.text: First confirm Connected near the top of Browser setup. Then switch on recording. It is off by default; a disabled switch means no live connection.

notes.title: Safari is not enabled yet
notes.text: No Safari setting will make this build record Safari. Packaging and validation require full Xcode and further implementation.

name: 06-preferences
title: Choose your recording preferences
kind: Native preferences content render · full content shown without the popover's scroll crop

notes.title: Launch at login is optional
notes.text: Enable it in the real app if you want automatic startup. If approval is required, follow the app's System Settings message.

notes.title: Choose an appearance
notes.text: System follows macOS. Light and Dark set SurfMeter's appearance independently.

notes.title: Choose retention
notes.text: Keep 7, 30, or 90 days. The default is 30 days. Shortening this setting removes older aggregates.

notes.title: Add excluded domains
notes.text: Enter example.com and choose Add. Subdomains are excluded too. Existing totals stay until deleted.

notes.title: Delete activity deliberately
notes.text: Choose Delete all activity, then confirm in the dialog. Preferences remain; cancel leaves the records untouched.

name: 07-check-dashboard
title: Check the recorded totals
kind: Native SwiftUI render · sample activity, not proof of a live browser connection

notes.title: Check Daily first
notes.text: A short eligible browsing session should appear in Daily. Positive durations below one minute display as <1m.

notes.title: Check the date range
notes.text: Weekly covers seven local calendar days, including today so far. Today is a partial day.

notes.title: Read the daily chart
notes.text: Each bar is one day's recorded time. Gaps do not prove the browser was unused.

notes.title: Open website details
notes.text: Click a row for hourly Daily detail or seven-day Weekly detail. Returning preserves the selected period.

name: 08-reload-remove
title: Reload, disable, or remove the extension
kind: Google Chrome documentation screenshot · use the controls on your SurfMeter card

notes.title: Reload after rebuilding
notes.text: Click the circular arrow on SurfMeter's card after updating its extension files, then click its toolbar icon to reconnect.

notes.title: Disable the extension
notes.text: Turn this switch off to disable the browser bridge. It does not delete previously recorded activity.

notes.title: Remove when uninstalling
notes.text: Remove SurfMeter's extension, quit the app, and remove its native host registration using the guide's cleanup steps.
